text.text_excerpt: We came to Mimi's after hearing about it from a nice NOLA yelper at the Krewe du Vieuxing party. We had consumed some beer and needed to find a place to maybe use the facilities and have a seat for a bit. This place is tucked away in an area of NOLA that I have never visited and I really liked the neighborhood chill vibe. We found a seat, ordered beer, and hung out for a bit while scoping out our viewing options for the parade. Bartenders were prepared for the influx of people and were friendly while dealing with them. Upstairs was also really cool, complete with a balcony. Additionally, the door guy was really awesome about letting you back in with your stamped hand and they didn't mind ...

On a whim, I went to Mimi's. I read the reviews and honestly had no idea what to expect. First off, the Bywater is becoming my favorite place in New Orleans. Super cool neighborhood with tons of on street parking and really cool places to eat and drink. I walked into Mimi's after I park less than 200' from the door and fell in live that instant. Pool tables and and a great bar downstairs, then I walked upstairs!!! One of the hippest coolest rooms ever, exposed brink and warm lighting, hardwood floors and old French windows and doors. Don't forget it's cash only! If you do, they have an ATM. The small plates are incredible! I have the olives and the cheese plate, then the "trust me" which ...

Came here the other night with a friend for food and drinks. We sat at the bar upstairs and the woman who was the server/ bartender was SO NICE! She chatted with us throughout the evening and made sure our wine glasses were full and we were taken care of. We each started off with a glass of the vino verde ($7) as we looked over the tapas menu. Our server let us try a sip of the wine before we ordered to make sure that we liked it, which I appreciated since I hate when I wind up with a glass of wine that I absolutely hate.
